episode_title: CRB Program: Raising the Bar for Rental Housing

real_qa.q: What are the six key areas of the Certified Rental Building Program standards of practice?
real_qa.r: The six key areas are human resources, which involves proper training including health and safety and WHMIS; resident management, ensuring high quality service and communication; operations management, focusing on maintenance and building performance; financial and risk management, planning for capital upgrades; environmental management, covering energy, water, waste, and indoor air quality; and state of condition, ensuring the building is clean with proactive pest management and overall maintenance.
real_qa.requete: CRB certification six key standards areas

real_qa.q: How often does the CRB conduct on-site audits for certified buildings?
real_qa.r: The certification is valid for three years from the on-site audit. However, the CRB sometimes conducts random audits between that three-year period to ensure properties are maintaining certification standards. Generally, the full audit takes place every three years.

real_qa.q: What ESG benchmark recognizes CRB certification and awards additional points?
real_qa.r: GRES, which stands for Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmarking, recognizes CRB certification. Larger REITs and owners report into this benchmark by reporting their ESG practices and receiving a score on how well they perform compared to their peers. By being CRB certified, properties do get additional points in GRES scoring, and CRB is recognized as an industry supporter.
real_qa.requete: GRES Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmarking CRB points

real_qa.q: What training courses must all staff at CRB-certified properties complete?
real_qa.r: All property staff must complete three training courses: environmental leadership training, accessibility training, and diversity training. These courses focus on the program standards itself, environmental best practices, and accessibility and diversity principles.

real_qa.q: What environmental features are part of the Living Green Together designation for CRB buildings?
real_qa.r: Living Green Together refers to the environmental standards within the CRB program, which include an environmental policy, an environmental preferred purchasing policy, LED lighting or low flow fixtures, a waste management program, and products with low volatile organic compounds (VOCs). All CRB-certified buildings are automatically Living Green Together certified.
real_qa.requete: Living Green Together CRB environmental standards features

real_qa.q: What is the certification process for landlords seeking CRB certification?
real_qa.r: The process begins with registration, followed by a gap analysis to identify which standards are already in place and what is missing. Next, all staff complete the three required training courses. Landlords then review the on-site audit checklist by walking through their building, make any necessary upgrades, and schedule the on-site audit. After receiving the audit report and resolving any identified deficiencies with evidence, the property becomes officially certified.
